admission.justification: Five tests pin the incoming-first ordering and each grammar exclusion, so a future region change that keeps a fenced or escaped line as evidence fails before it lands.

applicability: Conflict regions with an empty base part whose differing lines are all real trailing-marker evidence lines.
conditions: Each differing line is judged in its own side's full-document grammar.
Lines identical on both sides are kept once as shared context.
exclusions: Regions with a non-empty base part.
Lines inside fences, multiline code spans or escapes.
Regions with any non-evidence differing line.

evidence: Rationale: each differing line is judged in its own side's full-document grammar (fences, multiline code spans, escapes) via the evidence table, with the trailing bracket required to be a real marker at its exact position; lines identical on both sides stay once as shared context; the plain/diff3 presentations must agree up to ordered subsequence so the diff3 base part belongs to the conflict. Unknown line texts never qualify, so automatic resolution cannot broaden past evidence. Observed: test_real_trailing_markers_still_resolve_with_shared_context (incoming-then-own, kept 2), test_fenced_code_lines_never_resolve_evidence_conflicts, test_escaped_trailing_brackets_never_resolve_evidence_conflicts, test_multiline_code_spans_never_resolve_evidence_conflicts, empty-base order in the F01 test.

statement: Rule 6 evidence lines: a conflict region with an empty base part whose differing lines are all real trailing-marker evidence lines resolves incoming-then-own; fenced, code-span and escaped brackets never qualify
